What is a Copilot Notebook?

A notebook turns your files and chats into one workspace that Copilot reads, summarises and reshapes into study material. Every screenshot here uses a notebook called Software Engineering, built from a 12-week module slide deck.

  • Create a notebook and add your own reference files
  • Ask Copilot questions that are answered from your files
  • Generate an infographic, a mind map and a full study guide in a few clicks

Create your notebook

Steps 1 to 3

1

Open Notebooks

Open Copilot and look at the left sidebar. Notebooks sits below Agents. Select it, then choose to create a new notebook.

2

Name your notebook

A window called Let's build your notebook opens. Type a name based on your work or topic, for example Software Engineering. The Next button stays grey until you type a name. You can rename the notebook at any time.

3

Add references

References are the files Copilot is allowed to use. Choose content related to your work so Copilot stays focused on what matters. You can add more later.

  • References tab: files, emails and links from your account, or Upload files from your device
  • Copilot Chats tab: past chats you want to include
  • Select the files you need, then click Create

Tip Pick the smallest set of files that covers your topic. Fewer, relevant references give more accurate answers.

Work inside your notebook

Steps 4 to 6

4

Chat with your notebook

Your notebook opens with a prompt box on the left and a Content panel on the right. The panel lists your Creations (things Copilot makes) and your References (your files). Type a question in the prompt box, for example Give me the summary of this module.

Copilot answers from your references and shows the notebook name above your question, so you can see which sources it used.

5

Create an infographic

In the Content panel, select Infographic. A tooltip confirms it will create an infographic from your notebook content. The result is saved under Creations as Infographic 1. Select Download to keep a copy.

6

Explore More in OneNote

The More in OneNote button, next to New Page and Infographic, shows what else you can create in OneNote.

Tip Anything you create appears under Creations and can be referenced by Copilot in later questions.

Study tools

Steps 7 to 10

7

Read the Overview

The Overview page is dated and has a refresh icon. It shows a Summary of the whole notebook and Key Insights grouped under headings. Small numbered tags link each statement back to the reference it came from. Use the thumbs up and thumbs down to rate the result.

The Quick Create row gives one-click shortcuts: Mind map, Study guide and Infographic.

8

Build a mind map

Select Mind map in Quick Create. Copilot draws your topic as a tree: the notebook name in the centre and main branches around it. A number on a branch shows how many sub-topics are folded inside, so select it to expand. Use Export to save the map.

Watch the date A mind map is only available for a limited time. The one in our example showed an expiry date about a month ahead, so export it if you want to keep it.

9

Create a study guide

Select Study guide (marked Preview). Choose the pages you want, then click Next. Summary is ticked by default. Tick all six to get the full set.

Page typeWhat you get
SummaryA complete learning summary of the notebook
Topic pagesA breakdown of the key topics in the subject
FlashcardsCards to help memorise key terms
QuizQuestions to test your knowledge (Preview)
Fill in the BlanksDefinitions and sentences to complete
MatchingA game for matching terms with definitions
10

Open your study guide pages

After you click Next, Copilot builds one page for each type you ticked. They appear in the Created content list as Study Guide: Summary, Fill in the Blanks, Quiz, Flashcards and Matching, plus topic pages named after the module areas. Select a page to open it.

Quiz

The quiz opens as a Microsoft Forms quiz, here titled Software Engineering: 12-Week Review Quiz. Choose the best answer unless a question says to select all that apply.

Privacy note The form warns you that the owner will see your name and email address when you submit.

Topic pages

Each topic page opens with an overview and a Why this matters section, then a Glossary table of terms and definitions. Numbered source tags link back to your references.

Tip This page itself notes that the supplied content does not give more detailed definitions, so check anything important against your lecture material.

Quick reference

Where to find things, at a glance

I want to...Go to...
Start a new notebookSidebar, then Notebooks
Add or change my filesContent panel, then References or Add references
Ask a question about my filesPrompt box on the notebook home page
See a summary and key insightsOverview page
Make a visual one-pagerContent panel or Quick Create, then Infographic
See topics as a treeQuick Create, then Mind map
Revise for an examQuick Create, then Study guide
Find my study pagesCreated content list

Good habits

  • Name notebooks by subject so you can find them later
  • Check the numbered source tags before you rely on a statement
  • Treat every Copilot creation as a first draft and compare it with your lecture material
  • Export or download creations you want to keep
